title: The boundaries between coding tools, APIs, and consumer services

opening.headline: When talking to developers, when terms such as API or coding agent come up, I draw a line about how much I need to know to have a conversation.
body: In a meeting, there are cases where the conversation stops when a developer says that we can attach it to an API or that we can run it with a coding agent. You don't need to know all the concepts, but you need to be able to distinguish between the roles that the terms refer to in order to accurately convey your needs.

In this class, we compare a general user service that logs in and uses a chat window, an API that is a channel for a program to call a model, and a coding tool that directly deals with code and files. At the end, we will use examples of conversations with the development team to divide the parts that non-developers are responsible for and the parts that developers are responsible for.
opening.objectivesLead: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:
objectives: Can explain the purpose of coding tools and APIs
You can distinguish between general services and developer services.

screens.title: When API comes up in the conversation
screens.lead: Hover over or select an underlined term in the conversation below to see a one-line definition. Check the terms one by one.

visual.alt: A scene with the developer's speech bubble on the left and four cards with unfamiliar terms on the right.

data.text: The developer says during the meeting: "The document summary feature just needs to be attached with API, and code modifications can be returned via coding agent." Hearing this, I wonder—how much do I need to understand in order to participate in the conversation? I don't need to know all the concepts. I only need to understand what the terms refer to, specifically Roles are divided. API is the channel through which the program sends requests to the model; coding agent is a tool that directly manipulates code; and API key is a secret value used to identify the calling side. Today, we'll examine the boundary between general services and developer services.

terms.tip: This is the connection through which a program sends a request to the model and returns a result. This is called by code, not by a person typing it into a chat window.
It is an AI tool that reads your codebase, modifies multiple files, and performs development tasks for you.
A secret value that identifies the calling party. It is stored safely without being exposed to the code.
Rather than memorizing the internal principles of terminology, the starting point for conversation is distinguishing who is a tool for what.

screens.outro: Before we unpack the terms one by one, let's think about which term was the most confusing.

screens.title: Think of the most difficult term
screens.lead: When you select each question, the instructor's thoughts unfold. You won't have to enter or submit your answer, so think about it in your head first and then press it.

items.prompt: What terminology gives you the most trouble when talking to developers?
items.answer: There are many words that are not used in everyday life, such as API, token, agent, and terminal. It's natural for the terminology to be unfamiliar. What matters is not the definition of the term, but whose work the term refers to at work.

items.prompt: Have you ever been unable to properly convey your request because you did not know the terminology?
items.answer: When you verbalize a request, it's clear what result you want, but it's often unclear whether that result will be achieved by a person in a dialog or automatically by a program. Knowing this difference allows you to talk to the development team while looking at the same picture.

items.prompt: Have you ever imagined the difference between regular services and developer services on the screen?
items.answer: The general service is a screen that is entered into the chat window after logging in. The developer service is a screen where code, settings, and keys are visible. Let's compare in the next screen that even if it is the same model, the screens and responsibilities are different.

screens.outro: Let's start by comparing the screens of the general service and the developer service as a framework to contain confusing terms.

screens.title: Screens of general services and developer services
screens.lead: Switch between the two states and see how your users, usage, and results change.

visual.alt: A left and right comparison image showing the app's dialog box on the left and an API call code snippet on the right.

states.label: General user service
states.body: You log in, ask questions in a chat window, and read the answers. The user is the person doing the work, and the results are the answers and files that appear on the screen. Choosing and setting up a model is also done within the menu that the service has already organized. Since you don't write code, you don't need any development knowledge to get started, and your responsibility is mainly to check what you input and the results.

states.label: developer services
states.body: An API is a way for a program to send requests to a model and receive results back. The Anthropic documentation introduces two different development approaches: the Messages API, which prompts directly to models, and Claude Managed Agents, which are geared toward long, asynchronous operations. In Google's AI Studio, Get code lets you replace the same prompt with calling code. This means that even the same model can be used as an app or as a part of my product. In this case, the user is the developer who creates the code, the output is a function within my service, and the user is responsible for storing the key and the calling code.

screens.outro: Now that we've differentiated between the two approaches, let's see where coding tools fall on this map.

screens.title: What do coding tools replace?
screens.lead: Select each tab to see how coding tools differ from regular conversations and compare the roles of the three tools.

tabs.label: Claude Code
tabs.body: Claude Code is an AI coding assistant that helps you implement features, fix bugs, and automate development tasks. Understand the entire codebase and work across multiple files and tools. It runs in many places, including the terminal, as an IDE extension, as a desktop app, and on the web. In Terminal, you can edit files, run commands, and manage your entire project from the command line.

tabs.label: Codex
tabs.body: Codex is a coding agent provided by OpenAI that helps you write, review, and deploy code. Instructions are provided on how to log in and use your ChatGPT account, and it is included in several ChatGPT plans, including Free and Go. Although the name is different, it is the same type as Claude Code in that it is a tool that directly deals with code.

tabs.label: general chat
tabs.body: General Chat helps answer questions, write and summarize, and translate. You can show and explain code, but the focus is on the text exchanged within the chat window. Coding tools go one step further by reading and modifying files.

tabs.label: comparison summary
tabs.body: The difference between the three tools lies in what they do. General chat deals with text in the chat window, and coding tools deal with files in the code base. Unlike these two, API is a channel through which a program calls a model, and developers can use it to create new services.

screens.outro: Now that we have distinguished the nature of the tools, let us explain with examples the scope that non-developers need to know.

screens.title: Explanation: API terms non-developers need to know
screens.lead: The instructor explains step-by-step examples of conversations with the development team. Select the right arrow to proceed to the next step.

steps.title: situation
steps.body: The development team says they will add a document summary function to the API. As the person in charge of planning, how much should I understand and what should I deliver? There is no need to study the principles of the model, you just need to know what role it refers to.

steps.title: Step 1: Start the conversation by knowing that APIs are components
steps.body: Attaching to the API does not mean that a dialog box will be used, but rather that the program in my service will send a request to the model, receive a summary result, and display it on the screen. The model becomes the part that creates the service.

steps.title: Step 2: API key is kept secret
steps.body: To make a call, you will need an API key that identifies the caller. If your key is exposed, someone else can call it into your account, so keep it safe without writing it down in the code. This is up to the developer, but understanding why key management is discussed separately makes it easier to coordinate schedules and needs.

steps.title: Step 3: Quality and cost vary depending on model and input
steps.body: The quality of the summary and processing cost vary depending on which model you use and what inputs you input. Therefore, the planner must specifically indicate what type of document is to be summarized, how long it is, and what quality is expected.

steps.title: Step 4: Divide responsibility
steps.body: The business requirements and sensitivity of input data are summarized and communicated by the planner. The calling code and key management are left to the developer. If the document to be used in the summary contains customer information, the planner and developer must decide together which part to send to the model.

steps.title: Instructor's judgment
steps.body: Non-developers don't need to read the code. You can see the same picture as a developer by knowing just three things: APIs are the parts that create services, keys are secrets, and quality and cost depend on models and inputs.

screens.outro: Now that we have confirmed the understanding of terms and lines of responsibility, we will organize them into one standard.

screens.title: Criteria for distinguishing between general services, APIs, and coding tools
screens.lead: We will organize what we have seen so far into one standard. Please read this and think about which side your work is closer to.

paragraphs: General services are used as dialog boxes, APIs are the parts that create services, and coding tools are responsible for reading and modifying codes and files. The three often use the same model in different ways, but the people using them, the results, and responsibilities are different.

Which one I need for my job comes down to two questions: Can a person read the results in a chat window, or should another program receive them automatically? And is it dealing with text or code and files? If you read text in a chat window, a general service is sufficient, if you need a program to receive it, an API is needed, and if you need to modify code, a coding tool is appropriate.

It's enough for a non-developer to be able to distinguish between these three and discuss their scope of responsibility. Any further technical details can be filled in through conversations with the development team. If you come across a term you don't know, start by asking whether the term refers to the screen that a person uses or the path called by the program.

callout.label: something to remember
callout.text: APIs are the parts that create services. First decide whether your work is sufficient for a chat window or whether it needs to be connected with parts.

glossary.def: This is the connection through which a program sends a request to the model and returns a result.
It is an AI tool that reads and edits code bases and assists with development tasks. Claude Code and Codex are examples.
This is a complete AI service that can be used as a chat window after logging in.
Distinguishing who is responsible for what among business needs, input data, key management, and code.

misconceptions.myth: To use an API, you must know the principles of the model.
misconceptions.fact: You can talk to developers about the roles, keys, and costs of parts that create a service. Even if you don't know the principles, you can distinguish between demands and responsibilities.

misconceptions.myth: The coding tool is just a chatbot that only developers use.
misconceptions.fact: Coding tools are a separate type that read and even modify files. The scope of tasks is different from general chat where answers are given in a chat window.

misconceptions.myth: Apps and APIs are completely different models.
misconceptions.fact: The same model is often used in different ways. What changes is not the model, but the people using it and their responsibilities.

closing.lead: Summarizes what was covered in this class.
points: An API is the part that creates a service, and the API key that identifies the caller is kept secret.
Coding tools even read and modify files in your code base.
General services and developer services have different users, results, and responsibilities.
For non-developers, distinguishing between roles and responsibilities is sufficient.
closing.reflectionLead: The following questions are for self-thinking purposes only and will not be submitted or graded.
closing.reflection: Is my job enough to have a chat window, or does it need to be connected with parts?

checks.q: What is the biggest difference between a coding tool and a regular chat service?
options: It even reads and modifies files in the code base.
Shorten the answer so that only developers can see it.
Always operates by entering the API key without a dialog box.
Only one model can be used without the other model
checks.explain: Coding tools like Claude Code or Codex understand multiple files and directly perform tasks such as implementing features and fixing bugs.

wrong.1: The difference is not the length of your answer, but the scope of what you do.
wrong.2: Input methods vary in many places (terminal, IDE, web, etc.) and do not work with API keys alone.
wrong.3: The number of models used is not a criterion to differentiate between the two types.

checks.intro: Check out for yourself the nature of the coding tool you just saw. Results are not recorded, and commentary appears immediately after you select an option.

checks.q: The development team says, ‘We will add the document summary function to the API.’ What is the most appropriate role for a planner?
options: Directly responsible for managing the calling code and API keys
Conversation begins only after learning all the internal principles of the model.
Organize and communicate business requirements and sensitivity of input data
Since the API is the same as a general service, I don't think there is a need for separate discussion.
checks.explain: Call code and key management is the responsibility of the developer, while the planner is responsible for business needs and sensitivity of input data. If you know the role of the API as a part, you can have a conversation.

wrong.0: Code and key management is the responsibility of the developer.
wrong.1: There is no need to know all the model principles; it is enough to distinguish roles and responsibilities.
wrong.3: API is a part that creates a service, so the topic to discuss is different from using a chat window.
